inspiration: Water surface as a sum of a few directional Gerstner waves, phase driven by a tick counter, with a floor on the amplitude so calm water still moves (shader/water/gerstner_wave.glsl:17-32). Recreate with three or four waves in our water shader.

Water is split into separate passes: underwater view, reflection and a mesh path (shader/water/underwater.frag, water_reflection.frag, water_reflection.mesh). A separate underwater pass is a clear look change for a shallow pool.

Sky from precomputed look-up tables: transmittance, multiple scattering, sky-view and clouds (shader/sky/*.frag and *.comp; multiple-scattering approximation at sky_multi_scattering.frag:15, transmittance step at :58). For a fast browser, keep one sky-view table per frame and skip the rest.

Music as a small state machine: named music states and a tag set, chosen from the current theme and tags (common/gamemusic.h:8-34). Recreate as zone and combat cue states with tags for mood, with crossfades on zone border.

Entities as instances of a script symbol: a world NPC is created from an instance id and binds to a symbol in the script VM (common/world/objects/npc.cpp:182-194, :264). Our catalogue pattern: one data row per instance, one class-like template per type (rows 20-21).

Light and fog effects by name only (not read): epipolar light shafts (shader/epipolar/), volumetric and virtual shadow passes (shader/virtual_shadow/), screen-space ambient occlusion (shader/ssao/). Look at the shader bodies before choosing any one for our look.

briefs.label: Calm lake surface
briefs.why: A few crossed waves plus an amplitude floor make a flat lake move without any texture; the surface reads from the sun glint alone.
briefs.keep: three or four directional waves summed in the shader; phase from the tick counter; amplitude floor so calm water still moves
briefs.change: our own wave directions and count; a shoreline foam band from depth instead of none; our own palette, not the donor's blue-green

briefs.label: Dusk sky with a sun disc
briefs.why: A precomputed sky-view table gives a horizon colour that changes with sun height; one table per frame is cheap for a browser.
briefs.keep: sky from a look-up table; a sun disc drawn over the sky
briefs.change: our own sun direction and palette per zone; no volumetric cloud layer; a stylised horizon band
briefs.ref: shader/sky/sky_multi_scattering.frag:15 and :58; shader/sky/sun.frag (name only, not read)

briefs.label: Zone mood music cue
briefs.why: One state chosen from a theme and tags lets a single cue set cover many places; the game can change mood without a new track for each place.
briefs.keep: named music states; tags such as place or danger; one selector that picks the cue
briefs.change: our own cue names and tags tied to the zone data; add a stinger on boss intro; no copy of the donor's track set
